summary: Defines an experimental Mobility Header message and an option that can be used to try out extensions to Mobile IPv6. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: This reserves a spare envelope and note slot in Mobile IPv6 so people can try out new ideas without clashing with real ones.

questions: how to experiment with mobile ipv6
what is the mobile ipv6 experimental message
subtitle: Spare message and option types so people can experiment with Mobile IPv6 without grabbing real code points.

tldr.problem: Experimenters extending Mobile IPv6 often borrow unassigned values for new messages, which causes clashes when the same value is later assigned or the experiment gets deployed.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines one Experimental Mobility Header message (type 11) and one Experimental Mobility option (type 18) with free-form data.
tldr.outcome: They are for experiments only: implementations MUST NOT be released or deployed with them, and successful experiments should be standardized with new code points.

sections.title: Why Reserve Experimental Code Points
sections.content:
To experiment with a protocol, you need a protocol number, a new message or an option to carry your data. Most implementations pick unassigned values, which causes trouble when the same value is later assigned through IETF standards action or by IANA, or when the implementation is deployed. So the RFC says it is good practice to set aside code points for experimental use. The need is shown in RFC 3692.

This document does that for Mobile IPv6. The messages should be used strictly for experiments, successful experiments should be standardized in the IETF, and an implementation MUST NOT be released or deployed with the experimental messages.
sections.plainLanguage: If everyone scribbles their test ideas on any blank page they find, they will overwrite each other. So this sets aside one page just for testing.

sections.title: How the Messages Behave
sections.content:
The Experimental Mobility message can be sent at any time by the mobile node, the home agent or the correspondent node. Mobility Header messages cannot be combined, so there is always only one in any Mobile IPv6 packet.

A home agent or correspondent node that does not recognize the message type discards it and sends a Binding Error message (RFC 3775) with the Status field set to 2 (unrecognized MH Type value). A mobile node that does not recognize it should discard it and send an ICMP Parameter problem with code 0. Mobility options can be skipped if not recognized.

The messages can also be used for Network Mobility (NEMO, RFC 3963) and Proxy Mobile IPv6, since those also use Mobility Header messages.
sections.plainLanguage: If a device does not understand the test message, it just ignores it politely, and some devices send back a short note saying so.

sections.title: The Experimental Mobility Header Message
sections.content:
The message is based on the Mobility Header of Section 6.1 of RFC 3775. It has no fields beyond the required Mobility Header ones: Payload Proto, Header Len, MH Type, Reserved and Checksum, which RFC 3775 describes. The MH Type value marks it as experimental.

The Message Data field carries data specific to the experiment. If no data is present, two bytes of padding are required, and Header Len is set to 0 because the first 8 octets are excluded when calculating the length.
sections.plainLanguage: It is a normal Mobile IPv6 envelope with a label saying "experiment", and an empty space inside for whatever you want to test.

sections.title: The Experimental Mobility Option
sections.content:
The Experimental Mobility option can be included in any Mobility Header message. If the message also has a Binding Authorization Data option, the experimental option should appear before it.

It has three parts: Type, an 8-bit field marking an experimental mobility option; Length, an 8-bit field giving the option length in octets, excluding the Type and Length fields; and Data, which relates to the experimental extension.
sections.plainLanguage: If the message is a letter, the option is a sticky note you can attach to any letter to carry extra test information.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Protection depends on the experiment. If the messages carry information that should not be revealed or that can affect the binding cache entry at the home agent or correspondent node, they should be protected like Binding Updates and Binding Acknowledgements.

Firewalls and intrusion detection monitors rely on unambiguous readings of these fields. An analyzer that does not understand new values may fail, either losing connectivity if it drops unrecognized traffic, or losing security if it forwards it and the values are used in an attack.

Within one administrative domain, each code point must be used consistently. Across several domains, experimenters should assume other experiments may use the same code points at once and interfere. See RFC 4727.
sections.plainLanguage: Test messages can still be dangerous if they carry secrets or confuse guards. Because only one test slot exists, other people's tests may bump into yours.

sections.title: Assigned Values
sections.content:
The Experimental Mobility Header message has been assigned type value 11, from the same space as the MH Type field in the Mobility Header. The Experimental Mobility option has been assigned type value 18, from the same space as Mobility Options.

By design only a single code point is allocated for the message and another for the option, which limits experiments among a set of peers to one at a time.
sections.plainLanguage: The test envelope is number 11 and the test sticky note is number 18. There is only one of each, so only one test at a time.

fields.name: Payload Proto
fields.desc: Standard Mobility Header field, described in RFC 3775.

fields.name: Header Len
fields.desc: Set to 0 when there is no data, since the first 8 octets are excluded.

fields.name: MH Type
fields.desc: Marks the message as an Experimental Mobility Header message.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Standard Mobility Header field, described in RFC 3775.

fields.name: Checksum
fields.desc: Standard Mobility Header field, described in RFC 3775.

fields.name: Message Data
fields.desc: Variable-length data for the experiment; two bytes of padding if there is none.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Option length in octets, excluding Type and Length.

fields.name: Data
fields.desc: Data related to the experimental extension; variable length.
